messages:
maria: Heads up — customer AcmeHealth opened an escalated ticket: missing audit events in their SIEM after we flipped them to the new export/forwarder pipeline. They say policy.update and secret.access events between 2025-09-10T00:00Z and 2025-09-10T06:00Z are absent. They pasted two example event_ids: evt_01G9aX3Q and evt_01G9bY4R. They see gaps in Splunk ingestion and some TLS connection resets from our forwarder to their indexer.

ken: Can you paste the exact forwarder config they used and the export manifest? Also which forwarder version? :thinking_face:

maria: Forwarder version reported: 2.6.1. They used the default s3->forwarder->splunk path with manifestVersion v3. They attached a truncated manifest (sent in ticket). I'm pasting the manifest prefix we see in prod: s3://redwood-audit-exports/prod/acmehealth/2025-09-10/manifest.json

alice: Quick checklist: 1) Check whether those event_ids exist in raw S3 blobs under that prefix. 2) Ensure the forwarder pod logs don't show KMS decrypt errors (we saw similar with older versions). 3) Check transform/field-normalization step for dropped events due to unexpected schema changes.

andrew: I grep'd the S3 objects for that day and the two event_ids are present in raw gz blobs (I pulled one sample). So export to S3 seems fine. That suggests the issue is between forwarder and the splunk sink or in the transform filter.

maria: Customer says Splunk shows connection resets 02:10-02:17Z. They also see a small subset of events that were forwarded but missing the policy.action field (schema shift). Could the forwarder be silently dropping events that don't match the normalization schema?

sre-bot: Note: forwarder-deployment/forwarder-2.6.1 restarted 2025-09-10T02:12:34Z in us-west-2 due to OOMKilled.

ken: OOM restart would explain a window of dropped events. But not partial field drops. We have some heuristics: if a transform raises an exception, we either drop+log or fallback to passthrough depending on config. Which mode is set for that customer?

maria: Their profile is set to "strict_schema_filter": true (enterprise default). That would drop events that fail normalization and log them to /var/log/forwarder/dropped_events.log in the pod. I didn't see that file in the ticket attachment.

alice: Steps to repro / triage:
1) From support playground, fetch the S3 object list for that prefix and search for event ids:
```bash
aws s3 ls s3://redwood-audit-exports/prod/acmehealth/2025-09-10/ --recursive | grep '2025-09-10'
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-audit-exports/prod/acmehealth/2025-09-10/part-0001.gz - | gunzip -c | jq -c 'select(.event_id=="evt_01G9aX3Q" or .event_id=="evt_01G9bY4R")'
```
2) Check forwarder pod logs and dropped_events log:
```bash
kubectl -n infra logs deploy/forwarder --since=6h | grep -i dropp
kubectl -n infra exec deploy/forwarder -- cat /var/log/forwarder/dropped_events.log | tail -n 200
```
3) Inspect forwarder metrics for queue_retries, decrypt_errors, and memory_rss around 02:00-03:00Z.

maria: I ran step 1 and confirmed raw events exist. I also pulled forwarder logs and saw repeated stack traces from the normalizer at 02:11:XX complaining about missing field `policy.action` and raising KeyError. There are also KMS decrypt warnings earlier at 01:58Z but they resolved.

andrew: That matches my local sample — the transform code used an unguarded `.get('policy')['action']` at that version. Patch in 2.6.2 adds safe_get for nested fields. So in strict_schema_filter mode, those would be treated as normalization failures and dropped.

ken: Proposed mitigation: 1) Ask the customer to flip `strict_schema_filter` to false temporarily (non-blocking passthrough) so they get events while we roll out a forwarder patch. 2) Immediately rollout forwarder 2.6.2 to the affected shard in us-west-2 and confirm no further OOMs.

security-oncall: +1 to ken. Also need an incident note for compliance: missing audit events could be a reportable gap depending on customer retention SLA. Please record affected time window and customer impact in the incident tracker. I'll open the IR and mark severity P2 for now.

maria: I told the customer the short-term fix is to toggle `strict_schema_filter=false`. They agreed to the toggle and confirmed some events started showing up in Splunk after 10 minutes. They asked for a postmortem and whether we retained un-forwarded events — confirm we still have the original S3 objects, right?

andrew: Yes, S3 holds the raw exports untouched for 90 days by policy. We can re-run a targeted forward using the replay tool if customer wants historical re-ingest into their SIEM. That requires an allowlist since replays generate duplicates.

support-bot: Action items created: #TICKET-4853 (customer update), #OPS-1420 (rollout forwarder 2.6.2 to us-west-2), #IR-731 (compliance incident).

ken: After rollout, let's also add a telemetry check that counts normalization_drop_rate by customer per hour and alert at >0.1% with an automated note to security-oncall.

maria: Thanks all — I'll update the customer and attach the logs + suggested replay plan. Leaving this thread open until rollout completes. :eyes:
